title: Store it dry, clean and sealed, then prove it works

say: Store it dry, clean and sealed, then prove it works.
This is the video for Module 2 of Post-Harvest Management and Food Preservation.
For grains and legumes, three rules protect almost everything. Store it dry, store it clean, store it sealed. Each rule blocks one of the causes of loss from Module 1.

panel.heading: What protects grains and legumes
items: Store it dry: damp grain grows mould
Store it clean: insects start in dirt and broken grain
Store it sealed: no air for insects, no way in for rats
Then measure again to prove it worked

say: Then you check your store regularly, and measure again the same way, so your own numbers show whether the change paid.

say: Grain can feel dry outside while the inside is still damp. If you have no moisture meter, use the salt jar test.
Dry some table salt over low heat and let it cool. Fill a clean, completely dry glass jar about one third full of grain from a fair sample.

panel.heading: The salt jar test
items: Dry table salt in a pot, then cool it
Fill a dry glass jar one third with grain
Add two or three spoons of salt, shake
Wait about fifteen minutes
Look at the sides of the jar

say: Add two or three spoons of the dry salt, close the lid tightly, and shake for two to three minutes. Leave it for about fifteen minutes.

panel.heading: The salt jar test
items: Dry table salt in a pot, then cool it
Fill a dry glass jar one third with grain
Add two or three spoons of salt, shake
Wait about fifteen minutes
Look at the sides of the jar

say: If salt sticks to the glass, the grain is still too damp. Dry it more and test again. If the salt stays loose, it is dry enough.
Always dry on tarpaulins or mats, never on bare soil.

panel.rule: Salt sticks to the glass? Too damp. Dry it more.

say: Hermetic means airtight. Sealed in, the insects use up the oxygen, stop feeding and die. No insecticide is needed. But first clean the grain and sweep out last season's dust.

panel.heading: Filling a hermetic bag
items: Check each liner against the light for holes
Inner liner inside middle, inside woven bag
Fill with dry, clean grain only
Squeeze out air, twist, fold and tie each layer
Store on pallets, away from rats and sun

say: Check each liner against the light, and never use a torn one. Put the liners inside the woven bag and fill with dry, clean grain.

panel.heading: Filling a hermetic bag
items: Check each liner against the light for holes
Inner liner inside middle, inside woven bag
Fill with dry, clean grain only
Squeeze out air, twist, fold and tie each layer
Store on pallets, away from rats and sun

say: Squeeze out the air, twist each liner tightly, fold it over and tie it firmly. Store the bags on pallets, away from sharp edges and rats.

say: When people say the bags failed, it is usually how they were used. Grain sealed while damp, a small hole, loose ties, or opening the bag every week for cooking.

panel.rule: Do not open the bags often. Keep a small tin for daily use.

say: Three safety points. Fumigation tablets release a highly poisonous gas. Only trained, licensed fumigators may use them, and never where people live or sleep.

cards.d: Phosphine gas can kill. Only trained, licensed fumigators. Never in a house or a sleeping room.
Only NAFDAC-registered products for stored grain, used as the label says. Never field sprays.
Use clean water on vegetables and coolers. Wash hands and clean containers between uses.

say: If you use a storage insecticide, use only one registered by NAFDAC for stored grain, and follow the label exactly. Never use cotton or field sprays on food. Hermetic storage avoids this risk.

cards.d: Phosphine gas can kill. Only trained, licensed fumigators. Never in a house or a sleeping room.
Only NAFDAC-registered products for stored grain, used as the label says. Never field sprays.
Use clean water on vegetables and coolers. Wash hands and clean containers between uses.

say: And dirty water spreads germs, even when produce looks fresh. Use clean water, wash your hands, and clean baskets between uses.

say: Fresh produce cannot be sealed like grain. You slow its breathing and protect it from bruises. Harvest early, shade it fast, and sort out damaged pieces, because one rotten tomato spreads rot to its neighbours.

panel.heading: Cool and gentle, from field to market
left: Harvest in the cool early morning
right: Throw, drop or stand on loads

say: Do not throw it, overfill sacks, or stand on loads. Keep yams whole and ventilated, and dig cassava only when you can process it within a day or two.

say: Problems start small. Every two weeks, walk the store. Look for insects, powder, droppings, chewed bags and damp. Smell for mustiness.

panel.heading: Check your store on a routine
items: Every two weeks: look and smell
Every month: sample and count-and-weigh
Hermetic bags: check for holes, do not open
Fresh produce and yams: every few days

say: Every month, sample open bags with the count-and-weigh check. Grain that feels warm deep inside is a warning sign.

panel.heading: Check your store on a routine
items: Every two weeks: look and smell
Every month: sample and count-and-weigh
Hermetic bags: check for holes, do not open
Fresh produce and yams: every few days

say: Do not open hermetic bags for checks. Look for holes and loose ties instead. Check fresh produce and yams every few days, and remove anything soft or mouldy at once.

say: Last year, in ordinary sacks, Hauwa lost 7.5 percent, about 75 kg. This year she used hermetic bags and checked with the same method after the same five months. The loss was 1.0 percent, about 10 kg.
So she saved 65 kg. At about 1,500 naira per kg, that is 97,500 naira. The bags cost 35,000 naira.

card.title: Hauwa proves the bags paid
rows: Minus cost of the hermetic bags

say: Her net gain is about 62,500 naira in the first season. Compare like with like: same crop, same storage time, same method.

card.title: Hauwa proves the bags paid
rows: Minus cost of the hermetic bags

say: To remember. Store it dry, clean and sealed. Test dryness before storing. Leave fumigation to licensed fumigators.
Inspect regularly, and work out your net gain: the value of food saved, minus the cost of the change.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Store it dry, clean and sealed
Test dryness, never guess
Phosphine only by licensed fumigators
Inspect every two to four weeks
Net gain = food saved minus cost
